answer: When k bonded identities equivocate on correlated votes, pairwise evidence yields O(k²) attributable conflicts, so slashing rises quadratically rather than treating each key as independent. Under asymmetric capital depreciation, detection also applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate loss as the swarm grows, making identity-splitting uneconomic. Even at the nadir, collateral remains escrowed; a glacier of accumulated exposure cannot be hidden by dispersing keys across a garden of aliases.
